top_categories.workout_context: 95ft/mi signals a climbing-heavy course. Sustained sub-threshold and threshold work builds the steady power needed without turning the opening climb into the day’s hardest effort.
Race-pace efforts that mimic Gran Fondo Hincapie's demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before October.
At Gran Fondo Hincapie, changes in grade or pace can lift effort above threshold before it settles again. Over-unders train that transition while you keep riding.

Road-specific control matters at Gran Fondo Hincapie. Practice on mostly paved Blue Ridge foothill roads with: use smooth gear and cadence changes, accelerate deliberately out of corners, and settle quickly back into sustainable power for 85 miles.
At mile 60 of 85, glycogen is gone. This workout teaches your body to produce watts on fumes.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of Gran Fondo Hincapie. Train it until it feels boring.
8,040ft of climbing on grades that change every minute. You need to switch from seated to standing without losing rhythm.
8,040ft of climbing makes aerobic ceiling relevant when the grade or pace changes. VO2max work supports those hard moments; sustained climbing and conservative pacing remain the spine.
Brief efforts above sustainable power can come from grade changes, positioning, or closing a gap at Gran Fondo Hincapie. Train them without letting those efforts derail the longer pacing plan.
Endurance with intensity spikes baked in. Exactly what 8,040ft of climbing on mostly paved Blue Ridge foothill roads with does to your power file on race day.
Low-cadence force work supports 8,040ft of climbing when the grade lowers cadence. Practice controlled torque while preserving good form.

Steeper ramps, positioning, or pace changes on mostly paved Blue Ridge foothill roads with can demand short hard efforts. Practice them without compromising the sustained work that defines the course.

race_overlay.nutrition: Target 60–80g carbs/hour for Gran Fondo Hincapie’s 85 miles. Start fueling within the first 30 minutes — early fueling prevents late-race collapse. Bonking at mile 60 is a nutrition failure, not a fitness failure.
race_overlay.terrain: The course profile at Gran Fondo Hincapie rewards specific practice. Include regular rides on mostly paved blue ridge foothill roads with sustained mountain climbs to build confidence.

pack_summary: This 10-workout pack focuses on TT Threshold, Race Simulation, and Over Under to prepare you for 85 miles of mostly paved blue ridge foothill roads with sustained mountain climbs in Travelers Rest, South Carolina.
